title: Redwood Optimize v5 — PRD, Roadmap, Design & Pricing (Release 2026-02-20)
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:

Redwood Optimize v5 is the next major release of the Redwood Optimize product line focused on automated workload-aware cost reductions and quality-preserving performance improvements for inference. v5 combines smarter model selection, adaptive batching, KV/prefix cache persistence, and per-route quantization profiles into a single opinionated product offering targeted at production customers running sustained LLM inference workloads. The primary goals are to reduce per-token serving cost by at least 20% on typical production workloads, maintain generation quality (no more than 1% relative regression on key eval sets), and provide first-class observability and rollout controls to platform and product teams.

Background and Motivation:

- Customers increasingly demand predictable unit economics for inference as usage scales (SaaS feature growth, generative search, embeddings at scale).
- Previous Optimize releases (v2–v4) delivered batching, model/quantization recommendations, and caching suggestions. v5 is designed to unify these controls with automated runtime routing and conservative quality guards to reduce ops burden and accelerate value capture.
- Competitive differentiation: provide measurable cost savings with integrated quality guardrails and standardized rollout mechanisms that work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Objectives (OKRs):

1. Reduce average per-token cost across Redwood-hosted workloads by >= 20% within 90 days of GA for customers who opt into Optimize v5.
2. Maintain generation quality: regression <= 1% on customer prompt-sets tracked in Evaluate (per-customer eval harness).
3. Achieve 99.9% availability for the Optimize control plane in Hosted mode; 95th percentile optimization decision latency < 200ms.

Must-have Requirements (MUST):

- Runtime adaptive batching: automatic selection of batch sizes by route and model that respects per-route latency SLOs.
- Per-route quantization profiles: safe, validated quantization profiles (e.g., 8-bit Q4x, GPTQ variants) with a fallback to float16 if quality regression detected.
- Prefix / KV persistent caching: support cache warm-start across pods for repeated prompts with TTL and invalidation APIs.
- Quality safety net: integration with eval-harness to run quick regression checks on a configured set of prompts before promoting a configuration.
- Rollout controls: canary and progressive rollouts with percentage-based targeting, automatic rollback on quality or error budget breach.
- Observability: per-route cost, latency, and quality dashboards in Redwood Console; structured events for optimization decisions.
- API/SDK: single API flag to opt a route into Optimize v5 and an admin API to preview recommended changes in dry-run.

Should-have Requirements (SHOULD):

- Workload classification: lightweight classifier that tags requests (e.g., chat vs completion vs embedding) and applies different optimization policies.
- Offline recommendation export for Dedicated/Private customers (CSV/JSON) and IaC suggestions (terraform snippets) for model/quantization changes.
- Cost transparency UI with per-token delta attribution (batching vs quantization vs model-change).

Could-have (nice-to-have) Requirements (COULD):

- Automated retraining of small calibration sets for quantized models to reduce regressions in specialized domains.
- Customer-configurable optimization policies (aggressive/conservative) in the Console.

Design overview:

1) Control plane components:
- Optimize Controller: central service that ingests telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates, eval results) and emits optimization recommendations.
- Policy Engine: rule-based + ML scorer that ranks possible interventions (batch increase, quantize, model variant) by expected cost savings and estimated quality impact.
- Audit & Safety: gating layer that runs regression checks and enforces policy constraints (per-customer quality thresholds, regulatory constraints).

2) Data plane components (runtime hooks):
- Runtime Advisor: lightweight runtime sidecar/library that applies per-request decisions (batch sizing hints, prefix cache lookups, quantization code path selection).
- Persistence layer: shared cache store (Redis/Quicache) with TTL and observability hooks.

3) APIs and Configs:
- Opt-in API: PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id}/optimize { "optimize_version": "v5", "policy": "conservative" }
- Dry-run API: POST /v1/optimize/dryrun { "route_id": "r123", "duration": "24h" } -> returns estimated savings in tokens and potential regressions (per-eval set).
- Rollout API: POST /v1/rollouts { "route_id": "r123", "strategy": "canary", "steps": [ {"percent": 1, "duration": "1h"}, ... ] }

Design decisions and rationale:

- Conservative-first rollout: default policy is conservative to prioritize quality and trust. Aggressive policies are opt-in in Console. This aligns with our thesis that production-first behavior wins.
- In-process runtime advisor (sidecar) instead of control-plane only to minimize decision latency (target p95 < 200ms).
- Use of validated quantization profiles rather than arbitrary per-customer quantize-to-X to limit regressions and simplify support.

Quality & Safety Gate (eval integration):

- Each recommended change triggers a quick A/B evaluation against a configurable prompt set (default 500 prompts sampled from customer's stored prompt-sets).
- Regression thresholds: absolute metric delta <= 1% on primary metric (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-cosine or customer-defined scoring). Any recommendation failing threshold is moved to manual review.
- Automated rollback triggers: increase in generation error rate > 0.5% absolute or customer-defined eval regressions > 1%.

Operational SLOs and Metrics (concrete):

- Control plane availability: 99.9% monthly uptime (SRE owns).
- Optimization decision latency: median < 45ms, p95 < 200ms.
- Cost savings target: mean per-customer savings >= 20% within 30 days of opt-in (measured on a 90th percentile of route-weighted customers).
- Quality regression alert: if > 0.5% of active routes show eval regressions > 1% for two consecutive days, trigger a Severity 2 investigation.

Rollout Plan & Timeline (high-level):

- Feb 2026 (GA target: 2026-02-20): feature-complete beta to existing Optimize customers; initial GA for Hosted and Dedicated with limited Private availability via partner program.
- Mar–Apr 2026: ramp GA to broader customer base; add Console controls and billing integration.
- May 2026: Private full support and IaC generation for on-prem customers.
- Rollout mechanics: staged rollout by customer cohorts. Canary plan: 1% for 1h -> 5% for 6h -> 25% for 24h -> 100% (monitoring windows and automated rollback checks between steps).

Release checklist (pre-GA):

1. End-to-end integration tests for control plane and sidecar (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
2. Eval-harness integration smoke tests and standard prompt-sets validated (owner: applied-ml-and-evals).
3. Console UI for opt-in and dry-run preview (owner: eng-developer-experience).
4. Billing hooks to attribute cost savings and update per-route pricing (owner: finance-and-legal).
5. Security review and penetration test sign-off (owner: security-and-compliance).
6. Runbook & incident playbook for Optimize (owner: eng-sre).

Pricing & Packaging Notes:

- Packaging: Redwood Optimize v5 will be offered as an add-on to Redwood API with two SKUs: Optimize Standard (self-serve, usage-tiered discount) and Optimize Enterprise (SLA, premium support, Dedicated/Private features).
- Pricing model: percentage-of-savings charge combined with a small fixed monthly platform fee. Example: 10% of measured per-token-dollar savings (30-day rolling window) + $1,000/month platform fee for Standard; Enterprise negotiated with minimum commitment and support add-ons.
- Billing attribution: savings are computed by comparing actual per-route unit cost with a modeled baseline (baseline defined as float16 + current batching policy at opt-in time). Savings calculations are auditable with exportable CSVs.

- Discounts & credits: early-adopter credit applied for first 90 days post-GA (100% credit on optimization fees) to accelerate adoption and data collection.

- Packaging constraints for Private: for Private deployments (VPC or on-prem), Optimize Enterprise includes offline recommendation export and IaC snippets; billing may be contracted as a fixed fee or revenue-share depending on enterprise terms.

Console UX highlights:

- Route-level Optimize status (Enabled, Dry-run, Paused, Failed).
- Per-route savings preview (estimated USD/month) and observed savings after opt-in.
- Quality dashboard showing eval-set performance and rolling regression alerts.
- Rollout controls with step editor and automatic rollback toggles.

Engineering impacts and dependencies:

- eng-serving-runtime: runtime advisor sidecar, kernel selection telemetry hooks. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- applied-ml-and-evals: maintain eval prompt-sets, build regression runner. (Owner: Ethan Brooks)
- eng-developer-experience: Console UI, API docs, SDK changes. (Owner: Ryan Kim)
- eng-sre: SLO definition, runbooks, incident playbooks. (Owner: Arjun Singh)
- finance-and-legal: pricing model, billing integration, contracts. (Owner: Laura Chen)

Release Notes (v5.0 — 2026-02-20):

- New: Adaptive runtime batching with per-route latency-aware tuning.
- New: Per-route quantization profiles and safe fallback paths.
- New: Persistent prefix / KV caching with TTL and invalidation API.
- New: Dry-run API and Console preview for optimization recommendations.
- New: Automated quality safety gate integrated with eval-harness.
- Improved: Cost transparency UI showing per-component savings attribution.
- Fixed: Various issues around cache warm-start regressions and batch scheduling edge-cases.

Ownership & Contact List:

- Product owner: Maya Patel (product) — primary PRD and roadmap owner.
- Engineering lead: Priya Nair (eng-serving-runtime) — runtime and SDK delivery.
- ML evaluation lead: Ethan Brooks (applied-ml-and-evals) — eval sets and quality gating.
- SRE lead: Arjun Singh (eng-sre) — SLOs, runbooks, on-call.
- Pricing & contracts: Laura Chen (finance-and-legal).

Open Questions / Risks:

- Quantization coverage: which model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) are safe for validated profiles? Need to finalize supported-model list by 2026-01-15.
- Baseline definition: agreement on baseline for savings computation may require legal review for enterprise contracts.
- Privacy/regulatory: ensure audit logs and data residency for Private customers; potential for restricted mode where certain optimizations are disabled.

Appendices:

A. Example API call to enable Optimize v5 on a route:

curl -X PATCH "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/r123"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"optimize_version":"v5", "policy":"conservative"}'

B. Example dry-run response (JSON shown for illustration):

{
  "route_id": "r123",
  "estimated_monthly_savings_usd": "1250.00",
  "predicted_quality_regression": "0.2%",
  "recommendations": ["increase_batch_size_to_8", "apply_q4x_profile_on-model-gpt-neoX-20B"]
}
